unit.why: A single anecdote about R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta as rabbi of Kolbasov, unknowingly bribed by money hidden in his garment, quoted from Heikhal ha-Berakhah within a homiletic frame on the verse about bribery.

stories.start_quote: בהיכל הברכה פ' משפטים וז"ל והשוחד
stories.summary_en: As young rabbi of Kolbasov, the Apter Rav finds his opinion in a lawsuit inexplicably shifting toward the bribed judges' view. He delays the verdict and weeps before God, then discovers gold coins a litigant had secretly hidden in his Rosh Hodesh garment. He forces the man to confess, returns the money and refuses to judge the case, which illustrates the verse that a bribe perverts the words of the righteous.
